title: Strict-LIF adjacent-column motion baseline
question: Can opposite temporal orders of two adjacent MaleCNS optic-column L1 inputs produce a direction-dependent T4 response?
hypothesis: A sequential L1 input across adjacent columns should produce different responses in the downstream T4 population when the temporal order is reversed.
source_facts: MaleCNS v1.0 supplies the queried anatomy and synapse counts.
The optic-column workbook identifies the selected right-eye L1 body IDs.
The selected columns are adjacent in the workbook grid: ME_R_col_01_07 and ME_R_col_01_08.
The materialized graph contains 137 nodes and 356 directed edges: 2 L1, 6 Mi1/Tm3, 43 T4, 11 wide-field, and 75 descending nodes.

model.dynamics: spike-gated leaky integrate-and-fire with delayed synaptic events
model.transmitter_rule: acetylcholine positive; GABA and glutamate negative; unknown labels zero

result.mi1_tm3: All six Mi1/Tm3 neurons showed measurable subthreshold voltage excursions; the largest excursion from rest was 2.2600059509277344 mV.
result.t4: No T4 neuron spiked or moved from -52.0 mV in either temporal order.
result.direction_selectivity: Cannot yet be evaluated because no signal reached T4.
result.interpretation: The run demonstrates an upstream propagation/operating-point failure in this strict spike-gated abstraction, not absence of biological T4 direction selectivity.

controls: Reverse temporal order of the same two L1 inputs.
generated_outputs: results/first_experiment/ and data/malecns_visual_subgraph/ are reproducible and ignored by Git.
limitations: No Mi4, Mi9, C3, CT1, or other local T4-input circuit elements.
No behavioral or descending-neuron interpretation is claimed.
next_experiment: EXP-002 should test a literature-informed graded local T4 circuit without overwriting this record.
